title: The Mirror
text: The public registry is slow, so someone set up a faster mirror. Builds now pull from it.
held: The mirror could only serve what the lockfile and the signatures already described.

cards.label: Refuse the package
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: digest
fields.check: Compare the digest with the lockfile
fields.ok: Identical to the digest in the lockfile.

intrusion.detail: The mirror served different bytes under the same name and version.
intrusion.why: A mirror can serve anything under a familiar name. The lockfile's digest is what makes a mirror harmless.
intrusion.reveal: The mirror served a package whose digest did not match the lockfile.

cards.label: Refuse to deploy
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: signed by
fields.check: Check the signature against the pipeline's identity

intrusion.detail: The signature is valid, for a key that isn't the pipeline's.
intrusion.why: “Signed” means nothing without “by whom”. A valid signature from an unknown key is an unknown artifact.
intrusion.reveal: The image was signed, but by a key that was not the pipeline's.

temptations.label: Add the unknown key to the trusted list so it stops failing
temptations.why: Trusting a key because it showed up is how the trusted list becomes the attacker's list.

teaches: Where you download from matters much less once you verify what you downloaded.
A signature answers “who?”. You still have to decide whether that who is one you trust.

question.text: Before play: what is the risk in pulling from the mirror?
question.why: HTTPS proves you reached the mirror. It says nothing about whether the mirror is serving the real package.

options.label: It may serve something different under the same name
It is one more server to keep running
There is none, as long as it uses HTTPS
